newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-"BEAR" SCHULTZ RETURNS TO MAUL AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-"BEAR" SCHULTZ RETURNS TO MAUL AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Recalled fast bowler Brett Schultz returned from 16 months in the wilderness to put South Africa on top on the first day of the third and final cricket test match against Australia at Centurion Park on Friday.
Schultz, nicknamed "Bear" because of his burly build, returned figures of four for 52, South Africa's best of the series as Australia were bowled out for 227 after being put in to bat.

Allan Donald also weighed in with three for 60 and, when he had Ian Healy brilliantly caught down the legside by wicketkeeper Dave Richardson, he became only the second South African after Hugh Tayfield to claim 150 test victims.

For left-arm paceman Schultz, though, it was a welcome return to the bigtime, a three-wicket burst in the final session emphatically reviving an international career which appeared to have gone into reverse.
He was heavily censured on his last appearance against England at the same ground in November 1995 when he broke down with a buttock strain after assuring selectors of his fitness.

Further injuries and the rise of other bowlers such as Shaun Pollock and Lance Klusener then saw him slip out of the international reckoning until a hamstring strain suffered by Pollock in the second test reopened the door.

He responded by bowling Matthew Hayden through the gate in his fourth over of the morning and then took a difficult running catch on the fine leg boundary to dismiss Matthew Elliott. Even so, Australia would have been content at 64 for two at lunch.
Mark Waugh was bowled by Donald three overs after the resumption Australian captain Mark Taylor was caught behind aiming a loose drive at Lance Klusener.
Taylor made a season's best 38 in a painstaking three hours 17 minutes but still has not reached 50 in a test match in 19 innings spanning 15 months.

An 80-run partnership for the fifth wicket between Steve Waugh and Greg Blewett (38) revived Australia and threatened a repeat of their heroics of the first test at the Wanderers where they shared a record 385-run partnership.
But Blewett was caught behind as he attempted to cut off-spinner Pat Symcox and Australia slumped from 197 for five to 212 for eight as Schultz took three wickets in as many overs.

Top scorer Steve Waugh (67) was caught down the leg side by Richardson -- although replays suggested the ball had flicked his pad -- and Michael Bevan and Shane Warne were adjudged lbw in the space of four balls.
In the penultimate over Donald removed Healy and, in the next, Klusener bowled Glenn McGrath.
It left South Africa in with a chance of avoiding their first home series whitewash this century following defeats in the first two test matches in Johannesburg and Port Elizabeth.
